prompt: I wrote this article about AI transforming work for our company's thought leadership blog. Can you edit it to HBR quality? The file is at editing-hbr-articles-workspace/test-article-1-jargon-heavy.md

assertions.text: First paragraph does not open with throat-clearing phrases like 'In today's rapidly changing' or generic scene-setting
None of the banned jargon terms remain: leverage/leveraging, utilize/utilization, synergies, best-in-class, stakeholders (generic), 'in order to', 'at the end of the day', 'moving forward'
Hedge words removed: no instances of 'perhaps', 'it seems', 'might' used as hedging (conditional 'might' in specific scenarios is OK)
Vague evidence either replaced with specifics (named companies, real figures) or explicitly flagged as needing author input
Output includes a structured editorial summary with major changes, word count before/after, and remaining considerations
Passive voice reduced to no more than 2 instances in the edited article
